messages:
Incident Bot: INCIDENT ALERT — dns-resolver heartbeat loss detected in eu-west-2a. 25% of internal service discovery queries failing. Pager sent to oncall-sre.
PagerDuty: Paging Anna (oncall-sre) — please acknowledge.
Anna (oncall-sre): acked. looking now. can someone post quick impact summary?
Carl (support): Customer reports: multiple pods failing SRV lookups during deploys to eu-west-2a. A handful of webhooks timed out. No public API errors reported yet.
Anna (oncall-sre): thanks. initial check: control plane shows CoreDNS replicas in eu-west-2a moving to CrashLoopBackOff ~5m ago. kube nodes look healthy but /var/log/coredns shows repeated "failed to write to consul" errors and heartbeat timeouts.
Ranjit (netops): seeing intermittent BGP withdraws on the peering toward our consul proxies in eu-west-2a. Could be transient fabric flaps after the midnight maintenance.
Jess (platform): tagging as P1. queueing a canary failover to eu-west-2b resolvers now. rolling route-policy: prefer eu-west-2b for service discovery in 10s.
Mike (infra): prepping a quick restart of coredns-daemonset in the problematic AZ to clear potential conn leaks. will do a safe rolling restart (one pod at a time).
Anna (oncall-sre): do that, but do not evict all coredns at once. set maxUnavailable=1. Also enable debug logging for 10m to capture handshake errors.
Ranjit (netops): applied temporary routing rule to route consul proxy traffic away from the flaky peering at 10:12 UTC. monitoring for convergence.
Olivia (prod-eng): is there any risk of config drift between resolvers? we recently bumped consul TLS min version a week ago.
Jess (platform): good call — I’m checking consul client versions. two coredns pods are still on the old config due to delayed rollout. that could cause TLS handshake mismatches.
Anna (oncall-sre): Mike, kick the first coredns pod restart. paste command for audit.
Mike (infra): ran: ```kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/coredns --context=eu-west-2a --grace-period=30``` started at 10:15 UTC. pod restarted and came back Ready in 18s. logs show: "consul: heartbeat OK" then next pod restart.
Incident Bot: NOTE — routing policy applied: service discovery queries now prefer eu-west-2b for 10m to allow cleanup.
Carl (support): customers are seeing decreasing error rates on our dashboards. Current error slice: 6% -> 1.2%.
Anna (oncall-sre): second pod restarted. logs show TLS handshake errors against consul-proxy 10.0.45.9: TLS alert: unsupported_version. That matches the version mismatch theory.
Jess (platform): rolling back the TLS min version bump on the consul-proxy cluster in eu-west-2a to restore compatibility. executing config-revert job.
Ranjit (netops): peering metrics show stabilization after route change. no further BGP withdraws in the last 2m.
Mike (infra): reverted TLS min version on consul-proxy group at 10:22 UTC. waiting for agents to reconnect.
Olivia (prod-eng): quick test: curl to internal service discovery endpoint returns 200 now from a sample pod in eu-west-2a. SRV lookup test succeeds.
Carl (support): customer reports confirmed: webhooks that had failed are now retrying and succeeding. filing note to impacted teams.
Anna (oncall-sre): alert suppression: mute subsequent identical alerts for 30m. Keeping the channel for postmortem notes and follow-ups.
Incident Bot: Incident mitigated — resolver heartbeat restored in eu-west-2a. Switching to monitoring mode.
PagerDuty: Auto-escalation stopped. Anna marked incident acknowledged and resolved.
Anna (oncall-sre): handoff to Jess for root-cause and follow-up. I’ll add timeline to the incident doc and start an RCA draft: probable chain = peering fabric instability -> routing change + TLS version mismatch during staggered rollout -> coredns unable to handshake with consul proxies causing heartbeat loss.
Jess (platform): on it. I’ll include mitigation runbook updates: force-consistent-consul-client-version check pre-rollout, and a temporary gate to prevent TLS min-version bump during peering maintenance windows.
Olivia (prod-eng): also recommend adding canary validation that runs SRV lookups after control-plane config changes.
Anna (oncall-sre): thanks all. final note: we restored service without full cluster failover and avoided customer-facing API outages. adding post-incident actions and owners to the doc. :thumbsup:
Carl (support): adding impacted customers list to support tickets and notifying SLAs team.
Jess (platform): I'll follow up with a short postmortem and scheduled meeting for RCA tomorrow 15:00 UTC. tagging owners.
Anna (oncall-sre): closing thread for live mitigation. move postmortem conversation to #postmortems once draft is ready.
